description: Per-issue Agent watch (watching/muted): WatchEntry resource, command/projection surface, and dispatch integration (muted suppression + watch launches on the fixed event set).

tasks.title: WatchEntry resource: domain model, persistence, store with state machine and active-Agent validation
tasks.description: Build the WatchEntry data layer in the Agent context. Add the WatchEntry domain model + WatchEntryState { watching, muted } (mirror Agent/Domain/RoutingRule.cs), a flat-column WatchEntryRow + DbSet + EF config + migration (mirror RoutingRuleRow / the RoutingRules config block / 20260718100000_AddRoutingRules.cs), and a WatchEntryStore : IScopedService (mirror RoutingRuleStore) implementing the add/remove/list state-machine transitions and idempotency with active-Agent validation (reuse RoutingRuleStore.ValidateAsync's agent_not_found / agent_archived pattern via a new WatchEntryValidationException). This is the foundation every other task consumes; it delivers no UI or dispatch behavior yet.
acceptanceCriteria: WatchEntryRow is persisted with a unique index on (ProjectId, IssueNumber, AgentId) so watching and muted cannot coexist on the same triple; the EF migration applies cleanly (dotnet build + model snapshot compiles).

Unit tests against WatchEntryStore (using the project's IDbContextFactory fake per design/testing.md) verify the full state machine: add none->watching, add muted->watching, add watching->idempotent; remove watching->deleted, remove none->muted, remove muted->idempotent.
Unit tests verify active-Agent validation: unknown agent rejects with code agent_not_found and archived agent rejects with code agent_archived, neither mutating any WatchEntry.
ListAsync(projectId, issueNumber) returns the issue's watching and muted entries as two groups.
npm test (server) passes; C# build is warning-clean (TreatWarningsAsErrors).
tasks.output: WatchEntry + WatchEntryState domain model; WatchEntryRow + DbSet + EF config + <ts>_AddIssueWatchEntries migration; WatchEntryStore (add/remove/list + validation + WatchEntryValidationException); unit tests.
tasks.notes: See design D1 (flat-column side relation, not Issue-grain state) and D3 (remove creates muted unconditionally when no declaration exists — do NOT verify a covering routing rule). Unique key is (ProjectId, IssueNumber, AgentId); add secondary indexes on (ProjectId, IssueNumber) and (ProjectId, IssueNumber, State) for projection/dispatch queries.

tasks.title: Watch command & projection surface (server): API routes + issue read-model projection
tasks.description: Expose WatchEntry over HTTP and project it into the issue read model. Add Watching and Muted collections (default []) to IssueReadModel and a new batched projection block in IssueQuerier.EnrichAsync (beside the comments/attachments block) reading WatchEntry rows via the shared MohistDbContext. Add IssueRoutes.Watch.cs (POST add, DELETE remove) that resolve project + issue existence, call WatchEntryStore, and return issuesQuery.GetAsync (re-enriched model); mount it in IssueRoutes.cs. list needs no endpoint — it is the GET detail projection. Deliver the full server-side operable + readable surface.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/projects/{projectRef}/issues/{number}/watch transitions the declaration per the state machine and returns the enriched IssueReadModel with the agent in the correct watching/muted group; idempotent add/remove report the current state without error.
DELETE .../watch removes a watching declaration (or records muted when none existed) and returns the re-enriched model.
agent_not_found / agent_archived outcomes are returned with their machine codes and do not mutate state.

Spec tests (high-integration, server fakes per design/testing.md) cover the issue-watch scenarios: unique state per pair, add/remove transitions + idempotency, list separates watching/muted, and watch projection appears in the issue detail read model.
GET issue detail lists and single-issue both carry Watching/Muted when entries exist and empty arrays otherwise.
npm test (server) passes; build is warning-clean.
tasks.output: IssueRoutes.Watch.cs + IssueRoutes.cs mount; IssueReadModel Watching/Muted fields; IssueQuerier.EnrichAsync projection block; spec tests for the issue-watch command/projection scenarios.
tasks.notes: See design D2 (route calls WatchEntryStore directly, NOT IIssueGrain — watch is Agent-context-owned; deviates from the prerequisites mirror on purpose) and D6 (projection is a cross-context read through the shared DbContext). Mirror Api/IssueRoutes.Prerequisites.cs return-shape (re-query enriched model).

tasks.title: Watch dispatch behavior: muted suppression + watching launches on the fixed event set
tasks.description: Implement the issue-watch-dispatch runtime in RoutingDispatchHandler. Add muted suppression after the issue number is resolved and before LaunchRoutedAsync (mirror the archived-skip disposition: continue + LogWarning). Add a watching-launch pass after the rule loop, guarded by evt.Type in {stage.approval-requested, run.failed} and the presence of an issue; for each watching entry reuse the routed launch path (RoutedAgentLaunchContextResolver + RecordPreflightFailureAsync + IAgentLauncher.LaunchRoutedAsync) with the built-in watch prompt. Remove the rules.Count==0 early return so watch fires with zero routing rules. Enforce one launch per (event, agent) via a local HashSet when a rule and a watch coincide.
acceptanceCriteria: A muted agent's routing-rule hit is suppressed (no launch) with a structured log, and only on that issue — the same agent launches normally on other issues (spec scenario 'Mute does not leak to other issues').
A watching agent launches on stage.approval-requested and run.failed, and does NOT launch on any other event type or when the event carries no issue.

When one event both matches a routing rule for an agent and that agent is watching, the agent is launched exactly once (within-delivery HashSet dedup). Under unchanged dispatch configuration, replaying the same eventId does not create a second AgentJob (grain first-writer per source); cross-delivery source mutation (config changed between deliveries) is explicitly out of scope per design D7 and the spec.

Watch launches use the built-in prompt (event fact + identity directive), never a per-watch ResponsePrompt, and mark provenance (TriggerRuleId carries a watch:-prefixed value — a string-prefix convention, not a typed marker, per design D8).
Watch launches reuse workspace resolution and preflight-failure handling identical to routing launches (a preflight failure records a failed AgentJob).

Spec tests (high-integration, injected fakes — no real network/grain/orleans per design/testing.md) cover all issue-watch-dispatch scenarios. Because no single task owns the CLI->dispatch path, these tests seed watch entries directly via WatchEntryStore and assert the full event->watch-launch behavior (including the rule+watch single-launch and same-config replay cases), proving the dispatch capability end-to-end at the spec level.
npm test (server) passes; build is warning-clean.
tasks.output: RoutingDispatchHandler muted-suppression gate + watching-launch pass; built-in watch prompt; per-event (eventId, agentId) dedup; spec tests for issue-watch-dispatch.
tasks.notes: See design D4 (suppression in the handler, not the envelope-only evaluator), D5 (fold watch-launch into RoutingDispatchHandler, not a separate handler, so suppression and launch share one dedup scope; remove the no-rules early return), D7 (handler-level HashSet dedup — do NOT normalize the launcher's stable key to agentId, that would change routing semantics; the at-most-once guarantee is scoped to within-delivery + same-config replay, cross-delivery config drift is out of scope), D8 (watch:-prefixed TriggerRuleId for provenance). Seed watch entries directly via WatchEntryStore in tests.

tasks.title: Watch human surface: CLI command group + issue view rendering + Web read-only cards
tasks.description: Render watching/muted to humans. CLI: add MohistCliCommands.Issue.Watch.cs (BuildWatch -> watch add/remove/list leaves, registered in MohistCliCommands.Issue.cs); promote ResolveAgentAsync + AgentRef to a shared internal helper so watch add/remove reuse agent resolution; render add/remove via PrintMutationResourceAsync as IssueShow (idempotent state-as-truth) and add watching/muted sections to TableRenderer.Issues.cs RenderIssueShow (covers the 'Watch projection in issue detail' scenarios for CLI view). watch list renders a focused two-group view (watching agents / muted agents) consuming the same GET detail read model — NOT the full IssueShow (design D9). Web: add watching/muted to the Issue TS interface and two read-only CollapsibleRailCard entries in IssueDetailPage.tsx's reference rail (covers the Web detail projection scenario; operations stay CLI-only this issue).
acceptanceCriteria: 'mo issue watch add <issue> --agent <name>' then 'mo issue view' shows the agent in the watching section; remove shows muted where applicable; idempotent re-runs report current state (add/remove render IssueShow — state-as-truth). 'mo issue watch list <issue>' renders a focused two-group view (watching / muted) distinct from the full IssueShow.
agent_not_found / agent_archived errors surface to the user via the server code flowing through the response envelope (no CLI-side code mapping).
Web issue detail renders watching and muted agents read-only from the existing read model (no new read API, no in-page add/remove controls).
CLI tests cover the watch command rendering paths; Web typecheck + tests pass.
npm run typecheck -w packages/web and npm run test:run -w packages/web pass; CLI/server builds are warning-clean.
tasks.output: MohistCliCommands.Issue.Watch.cs + shared ResolveAgentAsync/AgentRef; TableRenderer.Issues.cs watching/muted sections; Web Issue interface fields + CollapsibleRailCard entries; CLI/Web tests.
tasks.notes: See design D9 (CLI conventions; 'watch' is overloaded — mo run watch polls a run, mo issue watch subscribes; nesting under issue disambiguates). Web rendering mirrors the prerequisites CollapsibleRailCard pattern (gated on non-empty). Read-only this issue per Non-Goals.
